lead: you married into them at twenty-six and in twenty-two years have not been in that house on your own. what you make of any of them has never been in the room, and that is what keeps it out.
sun: an in-law is on the list and never of the house, which is where the whole of this operates from. you had them sorted inside three years: which sibling everybody defers to and which one is obeyed, which household has been quietly funding the others since the mother died, which pair stopped liking each other a decade before either said so. nobody asked for a word of it.
moon: the cover went up early and nothing has come out from under it since: not the sorting, and not what one of those afternoons takes out of you. what holds it up has nothing to do with discretion. you are in that house beside the person who brought you or you are not in it, and the whole shelter is standing on that.
pull: twenty-two years in that family and nothing of yours has been in the room. the shelter rests on one person, and a single upright gives no warning before it goes.
tension: the one time you went on your own — the spouse away, the occasion unmovable — the same quiet you have kept for two decades came out as sullen, and two people asked whether you were all right. nothing about you had changed. an in-law standing beside their person is being tactful; the same person alone in that kitchen is a stranger with something withheld, and both readings are of one silence.
cost: in two decades you have not made one thing in that family worse, which everybody there puts down to temperament. nothing else is holding the cover up. whichever way it ends, by a death or by a separation, you will be in that kitchen with the whole of them read, no place from which to say it, and nothing over you at all.

lead: your daughter's account of you, delivered at nineteen, is that you were around and never quite in the house. it is accurate. this is the one group you have been in that has no edge.
sun: membership has always come with somewhere to stand — on the roll, in the photographs, and a step to one side where the seams show. a household issues no such place. nothing in it separates being a member from being present, so the half-step gets improvised nightly out of domestic material: the early bed, the errand that could have waited, the hour after the house is asleep.
moon: an enclosure has no outside opinion in it. a step to one side among thirty members reads as watchfulness; the same step among three reads as somebody who is not fully here, and nobody indoors has seen you anywhere else. so the reading your household took of you early is the only one it will ever hold, and nothing has come along to test it.
pull: the edge was always the place you could see from. the two people you live with have only ever met it as a door closing quietly at nine.
tension: twice a year it surfaces as a question about where you are, put by the two people best placed to ask it. outside this house the same conduct is why other families ask what you make of theirs. in here nobody wants a reading of the household. they want somebody in the room at seven, and accuracy about the people you live with is not a service any of them has asked for.
cost: arguments in that house do not get won by whoever is loudest, because a person standing a step outside a room does not raise their voice in it. your daughter grew up somewhere unusually calm. a body of thirty would have made up the difference; there are two, and both have only ever had the visiting version of you.

lead: twelve came in that autumn and you took two of them the whole way. the other ten remember you as helpful and have no idea they were assessed, or that it was finished by christmas.
sun: a new lot arrives every autumn, and the people in the middle of the place cannot tell them apart for a year. from a half-step off they separate out by the end of the first season: the one who is good and will not stay, the slow one who will still be here at sixty, the two performing an idea of the job to somebody in their own head.
moon: going ahead of somebody runs to a decade a head: the letter sent in the right week, the room you get them into, the turning that costs other people their thirties. two at a time is the ceiling, and there were twelve. so the sorting stops being a private opinion here and starts deciding who gets a decade of you.
pull: the read that decided whose career happened was taken in their first season, quietly, by somebody they thought was just being kind to the new ones.
tension: it gets around, eventually, that you have favourites, and the word is correct. what makes it unanswerable is the shape of the evidence: the two you took are doing well, which any reading of yours could have produced, and the ten were never given the thing that would have tested it. saying out loud that you decided about them in their first season, and were right, ends whatever room it is said in.
cost: one person gets a decade of exact attention from you and comes out at the top of the thing, which is more than almost anyone is given by anybody. the ten went off and did what people do. both of the ones you walked across are in the middle of it now, where seams stop showing, and neither can see the thing that picked them.

lead: she was in the first place you ever belonged to. that place has not existed for twenty-five years, and the line between the two of you has not gone slack in any season since.
sun: every room you have ever been counted in got read from a half-step outside it, and the readings stayed where they were taken. she is the exception. she was in the first of them with you, and at twenty-two you told her what you had of her, badly. she is the only person who has been handed her own result and given decades to answer it.
moon: what the rooms do not get goes down that line. twenty-five years of findings about people she has never met, sent in full, and she is the only one who has ever handed one back corrected. nothing about it is occasional. there has been no lapsed year to pick up from and no season it was allowed to hang loose, and both ends have been pulling the whole length.
pull: you are a member of everything and inside nothing. one line, running since you were twenty and taut from both ends, has carried every sentence the rooms never got.
tension: the people in your current room can tell there is somebody they have never met who gets all of it, and they read that as a reserve you are keeping from them. the harder part is calibration. every reading you have taken in twenty-five years has gone to one person for confirmation, she has her own angle on you, and no third party has ever been in a position to say which of you was right.
cost: six words to her do what a whole evening does for other people, because a line that has been under load for twenty-five years never has to be re-established. everything else in your life runs on turning up. if her end lets go, every body that counts you a member carries on exactly as it is, without registering anything, and that is the measure of what they had.
